assign.request: The worktree pool in Servex: take_worktree / return_worktree (brief: ai/2026-09-25/quickfix-worktrees/pool/requirements.md)

log.msg: Skipped the usage refresh: ai/usage.json is outside this minion's fence.
Servex/Pool.js written and wired (start, tools, GET /api/worktrees, SERVEX_NO_POOL). Slots come from the MAIN checkout's worktree-up/down, found with git rev-parse --git-common-dir.
Finding: a private Servex run from a worktree dies at boot on a missing http-proxy, because Servex/node_modules is not in a fresh worktree. Fixed with npm ci in Servex/ (same lockfile, nothing new).

Finding: Server/health.mjs allows one copy per machine through a lock in os.tmpdir(), so a slot's watcher would see the owner's and exit. Each slot's watcher gets its own TEMP/TMP; the proof shows health.mjs running under it.

decision.question: A fresh worktree is dirty at birth: its own server's PageFiles appends the page.jsonl lines michael/dev has not committed. How can an unused slot ever be returned or removed?
options: Record the slot's dirt at ready time as a baseline (file plus content hash). A return ignores only files whose hash is unchanged. On removal, stop the server first and put back only those unchanged files, then worktree-down.
Refuse every return and leak every slot on disk until michael/dev commits the lines.
git worktree remove --force, which the brief forbids.
decision.chose: Record the slot's dirt at ready time as a baseline (file plus content hash). A return ignores only files whose hash is unchanged. On removal, stop the server first and put back only those unchanged files, then worktree-down.
decision.because: The hash check means nothing an agent wrote can be put back. Only the server's own boot lines are, and every server writes them again at boot.

decision.question: The second proof run stopped Servex while two removals were still queued, and a half-removed worktree was left on disk, outside the pool file.
options: Keep a slot in the pool file's leaving list until its removal really finishes; adopt() at start finishes whatever is there.
Delete from the file only after worktree-down, which would show a removing slot in /api/worktrees under a state the Live card does not know.
decision.chose: Keep a slot in the pool file's leaving list until its removal really finishes; adopt() at start finishes whatever is there.
decision.because: It survives a restart, and the /api/worktrees shape stays exactly what the brief promised.

log.msg: Proof on a private Servex (8190, SERVEX_HOME in the scratchpad, no gate, no assistant, no monitor, no layers, no whisper, prefix qfp): 14 PASS, 0 FAIL. Proven on a private Servex (port 8190): 14 checks passed, 0 failed. See proof.txt.
